{{small|(29 March 2020)}} | updated = 9 May 2020 | prevseason = [[2018–19 Liga Primera|2018–19]] | nextseason = [[2020–21 Liga Primera|2020–21]] }} The '''2019–20 Liga Primera de Nicaragua''' season was divided into two tournaments (Apertura and Clausura) and will determine the 73rd and 74th champions in the history of the [[Liga Primera de Nicaragua]], the top division of [[association football|football]] in [[Nicaragua]]. The Apertura tournament was played in the second half of 2019, while the Clausura was played in the first half of 2020. The league was one of the few football leagues in the world, along with the [[2020 Belarusian Premier League|Belarus]],{{cite news |title=The country which does not fear COVID-19: "These things happen" |url=https://www.besoccer.com/new/the-country-which-does-not-fear-covid-19-these-things-happen-814188 |accessdate=28 March 2020 |publisher=Be Soccer |date=28 March 2020 |archive-date=31 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200531210141/https://www.besoccer.com/new/the-country-which-does-not-fear-covid-19-these-things-happen-814188 |url-status=dead }}{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52084121|title=Belarus league plays on amid coronavirus|work=BBC Sport|date=29 March 2020}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/mar/29/belarus-football-continues-coronavirus-premier-league|title=Last league standing: Belarusian football basks in new-found popularity|website=[[TheGuardian.com]]|date=29 March 2020}} [[2020 Tajikistan Higher League|Tajikistan]] that did not suspend their season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Nicaragua|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |last1=Flores |first1=Omar |title=Mexicans players in Nicaragua play through coronavirus outbreak as fear, uncertainty linger |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/mexico-mex/story/4079002/mexicans-players-in-nicaragua-play-through-coronavirus-outbreak-as-fearuncertainty-lingers |website=ESPN FC |accessdate=4 April 2020 |date=26 March 2020}}{{cite news |last1=Wagner |first1=James |title=Looking for a Full Sports Calendar? Try Nicaragua |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/04/14/sports/coronavirus-nicaragua-sports-events.html |accessdate=16 April 2020 |work=The New York Times |date=14 April 2020}}{{cite web |title=ФФТ ПРИОСТАНОВИЛА ВСЕ ФУТБОЛЬНЫЕ СОРЕВНОВАНИЯ ДО 10 МАЯ |url=http://fft.tj/fft-priostanovila-vse-futbolnye-sorevnovaniya-do-10-maya/ |website=fft.tj/ |publisher=Tajikistan Football Federation |accessdate=25 April 2020 |language=Russian |date=25 April 2020}} ==Format== The Apertura play-off format was changed from previous years, while the Clausura will use the same 4-team play-off format. For the Apertura, the top four teams from the regular stage advanced to a "quadrangular" double-round robin instead of a play-off stage. The regular stage and quadrangular winners would have played to decide the tournament's champion, but ultimately the same team won both and the final was not necessary. The same format was recently adopted by the [[Costa Rican Primera División]], but for both half seasons. == Team information == A total of ten teams contested the league, including nine sides from the [[2018–19 Primera División de Nicaragua|2018–19 Primera División]], and one side from the [[2018–19 Segunda División de Fútbol Nicaragüense|2018–19 Segunda División]]. [[UNAN Managua]] finished last in the aggregate table and were relegated to the Segunda División. The champions from the Segunda División, [[Deportivo Las Sabanas]] were promoted in their place. The 9th place team in the aggregate table, [[Chinandega FC]], faced the second place team from the Segunda División, [[FC Gutiérrez]], in a playoff for a spot in the Primera División.
